title: Bone regeneration with autologous adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells: A reliable experimental model in rats
author: Barrientos, Redondo, et al.
materials: The fat pad was processed as described in the literature with light modifications so as to obtain putative ATMSC [9], [10], [11]. The fresh adipose tissue was embedded in HBSS (Hank ´s Balanced Salt Solution) and disaggregated. Fragments were placed in a conic tube and washed sequentially in PBS1x + glucose (5 mM) + BSA (2%) to induce the precipitation of the non-adipose phase. The supernatant adipose tissue was washed again for complete removal of hematic and local anesthetic components. The adipose phase was then digested (1 h, 37 °C) in 1 mg/ml Type I collagenase A (Roche Molecular Biochemicals) and neutralized afterwards. The cell phase was centrifuged (1200 rpm, 5 min.) to separate mature adipocytes and the stromal vascular fraction. Floating adipocytes were removed, and pelleted stromal cells were NH4Cl treated (160 mM, 5 min.) so as to lyse red blood cells. NH4Cl was neutralized with DMEM + 10% FBS + 1% de penicillin / streptomycin + 1% glutamine and a new centrifugation step was made (5 min, 2500 rpm). After supernatant removal, the cell pellet was passed through a 100 μm. cell strainer before plating and culturing at high density (20–30.000 cells/cm2) in a 200 μl. solution containing DMEM + 10% FBS + 1% Penicillin/Streptomycin + 1% glutamine (48 h, 37 °C, 5% CO2 atmosphere). Then, wash with FBS was made to remove the non-adherent cells. Cells were maintained for 5–7 days and the culture medium was subsequently changed every 2–3 days. Cells were grown to subconfluence (confluence was reached after 12–14 days) and passaged by standard methods of trypsinization.

steps.title: Prepare adipose tissue
steps.instruction: Embed fresh dorsal fat pad tissue in HBSS, disaggregate, place fragments in a conical tube and wash sequentially with PBS 1× containing 5 mM glucose and 2 % BSA to precipitate the non‑adipose phase; repeat the wash to remove blood and local‑anesthetic residues.

steps.title: Enzymatic digestion
steps.instruction: Digest the washed adipose phase with 1 mg ml⁻¹ Type I collagenase A (Roche) for 1 h at 37 °C, then neutralize the enzyme.

steps.title: Separate stromal fraction
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the digested suspension at 1200 rpm for 5 min; discard the floating mature adipocytes and collect the pelleted stromal vascular fraction.

steps.title: Lyse red blood cells
steps.instruction: Treat the stromal cell pellet with 160 mM NH₄Cl for 5 min, then neutralize with DMEM + 10 % FBS + 1 % penicillin/streptomycin + 1 % glutamine; centrifuge 5 min at 2500 rpm and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Filter and plate cells
steps.instruction: Pass the cell pellet through a 100 µm cell strainer, plate at 20–30 000 cells cm⁻² in 200 µl DMEM + 10 % FBS + 1 % Pen/Strep + 1 % glutamine, and incubate 48 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Remove non‑adherent cells and expand
steps.instruction: Wash the cultures with FBS to eliminate non‑adherent cells; maintain for 5–7 days, changing medium every 2–3 days; allow cells to reach subconfluence (12–14 days).

steps.title: Harvest and count MSCs
steps.instruction: When subconfluent, detach cells by standard trypsinization, wash, and determine the cell number.

steps.title: Prepare porous scaffolds
steps.instruction: Sterilize two porous scaffolds per rat; optionally immerse each in 100 mg ml⁻¹ fibronectin solution and incubate 1 h at 4 °C, then remove excess solution.

steps.title: Seed scaffolds with MSCs
steps.instruction: Resuspend harvested ATMSCs at 2 × 10⁶ cells in an appropriate volume, submerge one scaffold in the suspension; optionally apply gentle negative pressure via a capped syringe to evacuate air bubbles and promote cell infiltration; incubate scaffolds for 2 h to allow cell adhesion.

steps.title: Create mandibular defects and implant
steps.instruction: Perform a neck incision to expose both mandibular angles; using a 4 mm diameter round trephine, create a circular defect in the right hemimandible and fill it with the MSC‑seeded scaffold; create an identical defect in the left hemimandible and fill it with the unseeded scaffold; label each MSC container with the corresponding rat ID before implantation.
